chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Bazofari narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Razin (the seller of fabrics), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had a female slave, and he had sexual relations with her, then he bought her mother and her daughter, he said: 'It is not permissible for him to marry the mother and the daughter simultaneously.'

key_terms.فَوَطِئَهَا: He had sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry both a mother and her daughter if he owns them as slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies that the prohibition of 'hamar' (simultaneous possession) extends to slave women just as it does to free women, based on the principle that consummation with one creates a barrier for the others. It specifically addresses the scenario where a man owns a slave girl, has relations with her, and then purchases her mother and daughter, rendering all three prohibited to him simultaneously. This ruling underscores the consistency of marital prohibitions across different social statuses in Shia jurisprudence.
